meta.subtitle: Validating automation risk against the global job market — the risk half of a shared, three-part research question
meta.research_question: How do AI awareness, career anxiety, employer-demanded skills, and automation risk collectively influence strategic career adaptation among university students in Bangladesh?
meta.scope_note: These two datasets don't contain Bangladesh-specific records or self-reported AI-awareness / career-anxiety measures (consistent with Sheet 1's decision to exclude geography as noise) — that half of the research question is covered by the companion dashboard linked above, which analyzes a Bangladeshi student survey. What follows here is the validation half: does the automation risk students are anxious about actually hold up against a broad, independent global labor-market sample?
meta.source_1: AI_Impact_on_Jobs_2030.csv (n=3,000 employee records, 10 industries x 20 job titles)
meta.source_2: global_graduate_employability_index.csv (n=3,500 graduate records, 7 fields of study, 2015–2025)
meta.team_project: Strategic Career Adaptation in the Age of AI
meta.role_note: This is one of three linked pieces answering the same research question. Your teammate's dashboard — The Mindset River and The Career Express — traces how AI awareness turns into career anxiety among Bangladeshi students, then shows which field each anxiety group actually ends up choosing, using a 3,156-student survey. This dashboard is the validation layer: it checks whether those chosen fields hold up against an independent, global labor-market sample — real automation risk, demand, and skills data — before the two analyses are brought together.
meta.companion_name: Strategic Career Adaptation in the Age of AI — Mindset River & Career Express
